mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q, or the effect reverses for more than two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) following two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1, or the effect is absent in more than three out of five such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following UNRATE > 5.0% in any month, or the effect is not observed in at least three such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following three consecutive monthly declines in INDPRO, or the effect is absent in more than two out of five such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL over two months signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise for two consecutive months, or the effect is not observed in at least three such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-on-month increase in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) combined with a simultaneous rise in consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise month-on-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise month-on-month, or the effect fails in at least three out of five such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market with upward wage pressure, which raises input costs and compresses margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE stays below 4.0% for four consecutive months, or the effect is not observed in at least three such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) for six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts demand for materials and services and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive following six consecutive monthly increases in HOUST, or the effect is absent in more than two out of five such recovery episodes.
